title: Signature Anonymity-Set Monitoring
description: Signature edition: anonymous systems monitor their anonymity sets — if the ring shrinks to 3 members, anonymity is effectively gone and the system warns. Anonymity is a measured property with a minimum, not a feature flag. This is a Signature original method.
method: Track anonymity set sizes; warn below thresholds; the system refuses to promise what it can't deliver.
usage: Set minimum anonymity thresholds; alert when sets shrink; grow sets deliberately.

demo.code:
print('ring size: 50 -> 4 (members left)')
print('WARNING: anonymity set below minimum (10) -> new signatures held')

title: Signature Group signatures with opening
description: Signature edition: Group signatures add an escape hatch: normally anonymous, but a designated opener can reveal the signer (for abuse cases). The balance between anonymity and accountability — members are anonymous to everyone except the opener, who acts only under defined procedures.
method: Sign as group member; verify membership anonymously; the opener (and only the opener) can de-anonymize under policy.
usage: Define opener policy before deploying; the opener's power needs its own oversight.

demo.code:
print('leak report signed anonymously (group: 200 journalists)')
print('abuse alleged -> opener reveals signer under court order (policy)')

title: Signature Deniable commit encryption
description: Signature edition: Deniable encryption lets an author plausibly claim a commit decrypts to innocuous content: two keys, two plaintexts, and no way to prove which is real. Under coercion, the author surrenders the decoy key — the real contribution stays hidden and deniable.
method: Encrypt with deniable scheme; decoy key reveals innocuous content; coercion yields the decoy; the real content is unprovable.
usage: Reserve for high-risk environments; deniability must be technically sound, not just claimed.

demo.code:
print('commit decrypts with decoy key -> "typo fixes"')
print('real key -> the actual patch (unprovable under coercion)')

title: Signature Zero-knowledge authorship proofs
description: Signature edition: Prove 'I wrote this' (or 'an authorized author wrote this') in zero knowledge: the prover demonstrates knowledge of the signing key or membership credential without revealing which. Authorship claims become verifiable and private simultaneously.
method: ZK proof of key knowledge or group membership; the verifier learns the claim's truth, not the author's identity.
usage: Use where authorship must be proven but identity must stay hidden (bounties, disclosures).

demo.code:
print('ZK proof: "I hold the key that signed release v2.3"')
print('verified: true (which key: hidden)')

title: Signature Attribution watermarking (for leaks)
description: Signature edition: The flip side: invisible per-recipient watermarks in distributed code so leaks can be attributed. Each recipient's copy differs subtly (whitespace, equivalent instruction choices); a leaked copy identifies its source. Anonymity for contributors, accountability for distributors.
method: Vary the build per recipient invisibly; record the mapping securely; leaked code reveals its recipient.
usage: Use for sensitive pre-release distribution; protect the watermark mapping fiercely.

demo.code:
print('build for partner P3: instruction-choice fingerprint f9a1')
print('leaked binary: fingerprint f9a1 -> source: P3')

title: Signature Anonymous reputation systems
description: Signature edition: Reputation without identity: anonymous credentials let contributors prove 'I have 100 merged PRs' without revealing which account earned them. Trust transfers across pseudonyms and contexts — the work vouches for the worker, whoever they are.
method: Issue credentials for achievements; prove credential possession anonymously; reputation composes across contexts.
usage: Design credential issuance carefully (who attests achievements); prevent double-spend of reputation.

demo.code:
print('ZK proof: "I hold 100-PR credential from project X"')
print('new project: trusted contributor (identity still hidden)')

title: Signature Anonymous whistleblowing channels
description: Signature edition: SecureDrop-style channels let insiders leak code or documents proving wrongdoing without revealing themselves: Tor hidden services, air-gapped submission, stripped metadata. The channel's security properties — not promises — protect the source.
method: Tor-based submission; metadata stripped; air-gapped review; the source's identity never touches the system.
usage: Operate the channel with real operational security; test it; protect sources absolutely.

demo.code:
print('submission via Tor: documents + code, metadata stripped')
print('newsroom reviews air-gapped; source: unidentifiable by design')

title: Signature Pseudonymous commit identities
description: Signature edition: The pragmatic middle: contributors use stable pseudonyms (not real names) with reputation attached. The pseudonym accumulates trust over time — code review, merged PRs, incident history — while the human behind it stays private. Open source's long-standing compromise.
method: Pseudonymous identities; reputation accrues to the pseudonym; the mapping to humans stays private (or with a trusted third party).
usage: Let contributors choose pseudonymity; judge the work, and the pseudonym's record.

demo.code:
print('contributor "foxglove": 142 merged PRs, 0 reverts (trusted pseudonym)')
print('real identity: known only to foxglove')

title: Signature Blind-signature code review
description: Signature edition: Blind signatures let a reviewer approve code without seeing whose it is: the author blinds the commit, the reviewer signs the blinded version, the author unblinds. Reviews stay merit-based — no favoritism, no bias against newcomers — while approvals remain verifiable.
method: Blind the commit; reviewer signs blinded; unblind to a valid signature on the real commit; bias eliminated structurally.
usage: Use for promotion-sensitive reviews; the process must genuinely hide identity (no side channels).

demo.code:
print('commit blinded -> reviewer approves quality -> unblinded signature valid')
print('reviewer never knew the author: no bias possible')
